long_biography.plain_text:
Georges Cohen built his career in information technology, rising through Capgemini before leaving to establish Transiciel in 1990. He financed the venture from savings and developed it into a large listed IT-services group. When Capgemini acquired Transiciel in 2003 through a share exchange, Cohen owned 37.4 percent and became a significant Capgemini shareholder. The reported offer value measured the company transaction, not cash received or a fixed personal fortune.

After integrating Transiciel with Sogeti, Cohen left corporate management and organized family investment structures. His private-equity activity spans technology, energy, manufacturing, mining, real estate and financial services, including a documented personal Robex shareholding and a later subscription to new shares. He has also invested in SquaredFinancial. These stakes support describing his current activity as investment management, but portfolio-company assets, mining projects and reported enterprise values remain separate from Cohen's own wealth. No current personal net-worth calculation is available.

uncertainties.detail: Numerous people share the name Georges Cohen. The official birth record, owner-input age and birthplace, Transiciel history, Geneva connection and later Robex biographies form a consistent chain identifying this owner as the French technology founder and investor.

Cohen left Robex's executive team, remained briefly as a director and then left the board in 2024. A subsequent personal subscription and another disclosed financial-services stake support current investor status without presenting him as a continuing Robex executive.

Transiciel created the original fortune, and the acquisition was a share exchange rather than a simple cash sale. The company's offer value, Cohen's former ownership percentage and his resulting Capgemini stake are transaction measures, not a current net-worth calculation.

Family-office sources describe investments across several sectors, and issuer filings disclose selected personal and family holdings. Portfolio-company asset values, project economics and corporate market capitalizations are not treated as assets personally owned by Cohen.

The founder-built mechanism is very well established. Some reporting says Cohen used personal savings, but public evidence does not fully establish his wider family starting position, so the broader Self-made classification is used rather than an independent-start subtype.

No dedicated Forbes profile was found. The existing French Wikipedia page is canonical and retained; searches did not verify an exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website among many namesakes.
Politics beyond minimal identity context, controversies, allegations, legal matters, irrelevant private-family detail and all vessel research are excluded.
